raw_response:
I'm 65 now, and I've been farming this same land for 45 years. My wife passed a few years back, and my son works in Shijiazhuang in some factory job, so it's just me in the house now. I only went to primary school, but I know this land better than any professor. I have 18.8 mu total — most of it I do wheat and maize, the double crop, which is 15 mu. I still keep 3.8 mu of cotton, though honestly it's getting harder every year with my back and being alone. I'm thinking this might be the last year for cotton, but my neighbor Auntie Li says the price looks okay this year, so I'll keep it one more time.

For the wheat, I'll plant in early October like always, right after the National Day holiday. I buy the improved seed from the agricultural shop in town — it's the same kind Old Wang uses, about 55 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's the 50kg bag with the three numbers on it. Then in spring, around Qingming when the wheat is jointing, if it looks a little yellow I go out with the spreader and put down about 20 jin of urea per mu — that's roughly 20kg, a bit less than half a bag. Old Wang uses more now, he puts almost a full bag, but I'm old and I carry the bags myself, so I do what I can. I irrigate three times: once right after planting to get the seeds sprouted, once in spring at jointing, and once at grain-filling in May. The pumping costs me about 30-35 yuan each time per mu, but you can't skip it, last year my nephew skipped the last irrigation and his wheat shriveled.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, usually around June 10th-15th. The window is tight, only a few days, so I hire the combine for wheat and the planter for maize — I pay the custom operator, it costs money but what can I do? I'm not going to plant 15 mu by hand at my age. I put compound fertilizer down with the planter, one bag per mu, and then when the maize is about knee-high I throw some urea in the row, about 15kg per mu. I irrigate twice for maize if the summer is dry, sometimes only once if it rains enough. Maize grows fast in summer heat.

The cotton... to be honest, it's mostly because I've always done it and the land is near the house. I plant in mid-April after spring plowing. I put one bag of compound per mu and that's it, no topdressing — I'm too busy with wheat then. Cotton needs more pesticide, the bollworms always come, so I spray insecticide two or three times and use herbicide once. For picking, I absolutely have to hire people. I can still pick some myself, but my knees hurt after an hour. I hire the village women, pay them daily. It's my biggest expense for cotton.

I watch every yuan. My son sends some money at Spring Festival, but I hate asking. I keep some cash for emergencies — last year I got sick and the clinic cost me 800 yuan, so I don't spend everything on fertilizer even if it might give a bit more yield. I'd rather sleep soundly knowing I have money in the box than gamble for an extra 20 kg per mu. Last year was okay, wheat gave me about 400 jin per mu, maize a bit more. I hope this year is similar, not worse.
